Money Representation

Understand the information carried by a Money value, including exact decimal amounts, currency identity and calculation scale.

Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

This document defines the information carried by a Money value.

Terminology

Amount is a conceptual, exact signed base-10 decimal quantity. Scale is the number of digits after its decimal point in a particular representation. A currency's minor-unit scale describes that currency, while calculation scale is selected for an operation; neither necessarily determines the other.

Requirements

  • MONEY-REPRESENTATION-001 — Money MUST contain one amount and one currency.
  • MONEY-REPRESENTATION-002 — The amount MUST be finite and exactly representable in base 10.

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Supports the rationale

    Exact monetary meaning does not require a universal currency-wide calculation scale ↗

    Mikhaylov Bogdan; Omorov Akzholbek; Izripov Iusup

    Exact decimal meaning is portable while representation remains implementation-neutral and a domain rounding policy is permitted, not universally mandated.

    Scope and limitations

    The paper’s common quantum is an application architecture. Applying it everywhere could reduce exact intermediate values prematurely. The reviewer did not validate its equations or worked financial calculations.

    Legacy / Illustrates a risk

    Preserve the magnitude of a financial value; do not silently truncate it ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Finite exact base-10 amounts supply the relevant value-preservation boundary, not a storage-column format.

    Scope and limitations

    This is a personal recollection, not a verified experiment or a universal statement about COBOL. No details from the withheld follow-up are used. Exact representability does not define universal database field capacity. The Open Questions in spec/money/representation.md leave portable precision, scale and overflow limits unresolved: this behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core. Unsupported amounts already have a portable failure category; this comparison does not set the capacity threshold or introduce an overflow code.

  • MONEY-REPRESENTATION-003 — An amount MUST NOT be interpreted without its currency.
  • MONEY-REPRESENTATION-004 — Sign MUST carry ordinary numeric meaning; domain-specific restrictions on negative or zero amounts belong to the consuming specification.
  • MONEY-REPRESENTATION-005 — Numerical equality MUST NOT depend on differing insignificant trailing zeros.
  • MONEY-REPRESENTATION-006 — An implementation MAY use any internal representation that preserves these observable semantics; this document does not require storage as a decimal string or at a currency's customary minor-unit scale.

    Scope and limitations

    This is practitioner experience, not a demonstrated equivalence proof or a prescribed migration architecture. CORE-005.3 addresses reproducibility from the same declared inputs, state and context; it does not by itself prove equivalence between an old and a new implementation. MONEY-REPRESENTATION-006 covers Money only. SPEC-COMPATIBILITY-012 classifies changes to the published FinKore contract, not every consumer deployment. The interview does not authorize workflow migration, a universal COBOL-to-Java transformation, AI extraction guarantees, new portable errors, or recovery of undocumented rules by inference.

  • The portable decimal-string encoding is defined separately by Money Serialization.

Invariants

The amount and currency form one value and remain associated through every operation; see MONEY-ARITHMETIC-002 through MONEY-ARITHMETIC-005.

Example

The following JSON is illustrative and non-normative; the normative interchange form is defined by Money Serialization.

{
  "amount": "1299.90",
  "currency": "EUR"
}

"10.0" and "10.00" represent the same numeric amount, although their presentation scale differs.

Invalid Examples

  • An amount without a currency.
  • NaN, positive infinity, or negative infinity.
  • A value whose amount has already been rounded without a declared rule where precision was lost.

Errors

Invalid components fail as defined by MONEY-ERROR-001 and MONEY-ERROR-002 in Money Errors.

Public construction boundaries

The finite-amount and valid-currency obligations apply when a public native constructor exposes a Money value, as well as when a portable parser does so. A constructor cannot expose NaN, infinity, or an invalid currency as valid Money and defer rejection until arithmetic or serialization. Invalid native amounts and currencies use the same component errors above. This is an application of the existing requirements, not a prescribed constructor shape.

Native exact decimal values need not use the portable plain-string encoding. In particular, a supported finite decimal with an exponent, signed zero, or trailing zeros remains a valid amount; validation cannot round it through the caller's arithmetic context or reject it solely because its native spelling would not be a portable decimal string. Native supported types are documented by each implementation; unsupported types are not implicitly coerced.
